title: Mastic Tree: Ancient Mastic Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: A Mediterranean shrub that almost nobody lets grow old, mapped here at up to 500 years, from an ordinary roadside plant to genuine tree size.
intro: Pistacia lentiscus spends most of its life as a shrub, a low, dense presence across Mediterranean scrubland that most walkers step past without a glance. Left standing for long enough, on the right ground, it does something else: pushes up a real trunk and takes on the shape and size of a proper tree, which is exactly why the specimens mapped here were singled out. The species is best known commercially for mastic resin, tapped for millennia from trees on the Greek island of Chios and used in everything from chewing gum to varnish. One specimen here, in Istanbul, is put at roughly 500 years old, a genuine outlier for a plant almost nobody lets live that long. Three mapped, in Barcelona, Istanbul and Palma de Mallorca.
